title: Add NVIDIA Asset Harvester to 3D Models Registry
author: sharktide
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `nvidia/asset-harvester` (alias `asset-harvester`) through InferencePort’s existing 3D client: one image in, Gaussian-splat PLY out. Existing `/3d` routes; no fallback or Pollinations-operated GPU.
- Charges **0.07 Pollen per generation**, multiplier 1, Quest Pollen allowed. Corrected from 0.25 using the [live provider catalog](https://api.inferenceport.ai/v1/models) and actual 0.07-credit receipts on September 9; prose provider docs are stale.
- Live provider smoke returned a 5.2 MB PLY with 92,826 splats. Local Gen live smoke passed in 63 seconds: valid finite PLY data, correct MIME/filename, identical cache hit, one upstream submission, one 0.07 Quest-Pollen debit, and one matching emitted billing event. Telemetry was captured locally, not queried from Tinybird.
- Verification: 24 focused 3D tests, 44 pricing/catalog tests, Gen/Enter typechecks, SDK/UI builds and Biome pass. Updated against main. No production deployment performed.

gist.headline: One photo, many splats
gist.blurb: The 3D garden grew a new branch: NVIDIA Asset Harvester turns a single image into a Gaussian-splat PLY. Polli checked the jar: 92,826 tiny splats, all accounted for.
gist.summary: Added NVIDIA Asset Harvester to the existing /3d registry as nvidia/asset-harvester (alias asset-harvester), converting one input image into a Gaussian-splat PLY for 0.07 Pollen per generation.
gist.impact: Developers can now call the existing /3d routes to generate downloadable Gaussian-splat PLY assets with Asset Harvester, including Quest-Pollen payment support and normal caching.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Asset Harvester as a cozy pixel-art workshop where a single framed image is fed into a friendly retro 3D machine and emerges as a sparkling cloud of tiny Gaussian-splat dots inside a labeled PLY jar. Polli wears tiny safety goggles and inspects the splats with warm amusement, surrounded by code-plants and flowers; a small CRT robot can hold the original image and excitedly compare it with the finished 3D object.

Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, dark purple (#110518) outlines, nostalgic but beautiful.
